AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: We assessed whether umbilical cord blood placental growth factor (PlGF) levels at delivery are associated with fetal growth.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: From a prospective population-based cohort study we included 3,461 live singleton births. Fetal growth was assessed by birth weight, fetal growth pattern, and fetal growth restriction (FGR; decrease in growth between the second trimester and birth of ≥40 percentiles). In all analyses the highest PlGF multiple of the median (MoM) quintile was used as the reference category.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Umbilical cord PlGF was neither correlated with maternal second-trimester PlGF (p = 0.08) nor placental weight (p = 0.18), suggesting that PlGF from umbilical cord blood was of fetal origin. Lower PlGF MoM quintiles were associated with a lower birth weight (lowest quintile -0.60 standard deviation [95% confidence interval -0.71 to -0.48, p for trend <0.001]) and a different fetal growth pattern (p < 0.001). Finally, lower PlGF MoM quintiles were associated with FGR (lowest quintile odds ratio 2.00 [95% confidence interval 1.25 to 3.21, p for trend <0.001]).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Lower umbilical cord PlGF levels are associated with lower birth weight, deviating fetal growth patterns, and a higher odds of FGR. Hence, cord blood PlGF might be a promising biomarker to determine deviations in fetal growth and FGR retrospectively, enabling follow-up of these neonates.

Article.ArticleTitle: Fetal Growth and Placental Growth Factor Umbilical Cord Blood Levels.
